goal: Introduce Vitest as this project's first unit test framework and land a first suite over the four modules the user named: src/flightManager.ts (state transitions, pause detection, track-derived duration — the "nasty test suite"), src/airports.ts (ICAO/CSV parsing and nearest-airport lookup), src/legMatcher.ts (planned-leg auto-matching, all ten reason codes) and planned-route matching (src/plannedLegClose.ts, plus the route-relevant surface of src/lnmpln.ts and src/flightPlans.ts). The suite must be deterministic, hermetic and fast: no network, no live flights.db, no writes outside the repo's committed samples/ (read-only) and tmp. `npm test` runs it; `npm run build` and `npx tsc` keep working unchanged, and the Docker server build stage — which copies only package*.json, tsconfig.json and src/ — keeps working too. src/trafficStore.ts, src/db.ts and src/ingest.ts are explicitly out of scope for this run.
frozen_decisions: Override the project's existing "no test framework" policy: yes, add one.
Runner: Vitest (chosen over node:test for DX — watch mode, mocking, snapshots — despite adding a new dependency).
Scope: broader first pass covering flight manager + ICAO parsing + leg/route matching (not flight-manager-only).
Explicitly OUT of scope for this run: traffic filtering (src/trafficStore.ts), SQLite persistence (src/db.ts), ingest validation (src/ingest.ts). Good candidates for a follow-up run, not this one.
sequencing_rationale: COMMAND PREFIX — every command in every acceptance criterion below runs under Node 20, i.e. is prefixed with: export NVM_DIR="$HOME/.nvm"; . "$NVM_DIR/nvm.sh"; nvm use 20 >/dev/null. The default node on this machine is v26 and better-sqlite3 has no binary for its ABI (.claude/ENVIRONMENT.md). Criteria name the bare command for readability; the prefix is never optional.

DESIGN CONTRACT — the Designer runs before Phase 1 and must produce design.md with exactly these numbered sections, because every task below cites them by number: §1 Runner and version (the vitest version pin and why, the Node 20 install procedure, and the rule that installing must not rebuild better-sqlite3 against another ABI). §2 File layout and naming (where test files live and the glob that finds them; how `tsc` / `npm run build:server` are kept from compiling them into dist/; whether and how test files are typechecked; and the hard constraint that the Docker server stage copies only package*.json, tsconfig.json and src/ — so tsconfig.json must stay self-contained and must not `extends`/`references` a file the Dockerfile does not copy). §3 vitest.config.ts (environment, include/exclude, setupFiles, isolation, timeouts, reporters, and the coverage decision — recommend none in this first pass; the project resists tooling). §4 Test-helpers module (its path and its exported builders: makeFrame(SimFrame), makeCandidate(LegMatchCandidate), makeHandCloseFlight/makeHandCloseLeg, makePlannedLegWithChildren — with the default values for each field spelled out, since every downstream task depends on those defaults being stable). §5 Faking time (the fake-timer configuration that covers both Date.now() and new Date().toISOString(), which src/flightManager.ts uses; the advance-then-feed-a-frame pattern; the rule that no test may depend on real wall-clock time). §6 Faking the module boundaries (the vi.mock shape for './db' — which of the ten functions FlightManager imports are stubbed, what each returns by default, how insertFlight issues ids, and how a test makes one of them throw; and the same for './airports'). §7 Testability seams in source (exactly what src/airports.ts must newly export so the CSV/ICAO parsing is reachable without initAirports()'s network+fs path, and how findNearestAirport is seeded in a test; plus the rule that NO other src/ file changes in this run). §8 Relationship to src/inspect-*.ts (they are kept, not deleted — CLAUDE.md documents them as the verification story; their scenario tables are ported into tests, not moved out). §9 npm scripts (`test`, the `test:watch` decision, and what `npm run build` must still do). §10 Determinism and hermeticism rules (no network, no live flights.db, no writes outside tmp; reading committed fixtures under samples/ read-only is allowed and expected).

PHASE SEAMS — Phase 1 is groundwork the design decides: the runner exists, and the harness that fakes time, the sim frame and the db boundary is written once and proven once. Everything after it is test-writing that imports that harness read-only, which is what makes Phase 2's dispatchers safe to run in parallel. Phase 2 covers the pure and near-pure modules (legMatcher, plannedLegClose, airports, lnmpln) — cheap, high-yield, and it exercises the helpers in anger before the expensive task. Phase 3 is the flight manager on its own, gated behind Phase 2's review, because it is the one stateful class in scope, the only consumer of fake timers and the db mock together, and the one place where a vacuously-green suite is the expensive failure. Phase 4 ships: package.json wiring, the test:watch call, README, and the proof that build and Docker's server stage are undisturbed.

PARALLELISM — T-004, T-005 and T-006 have disjoint allowed_paths and no dependency on each other; run them as three concurrent Dispatchers. Every other task is sequential. Test-file paths are listed under both candidate roots (tests/ and src/) because §2 has not been written yet and freezes which one is real; the two candidate paths for a given module belong to exactly one task either way, so the sets stay disjoint whichever §2 chooses.

package.json is edited twice — by T-001 (devDependency + `test` script) and by T-010 (the test:watch call, final wiring). They are in different phases separated by reviewer gates T-003 and T-009, so they can never run concurrently; that gate is the reason the double ownership is safe.

MODEL RISK — T-008 (flight manager) is opus: it is a stateful class behind two mocked module boundaries and a fake clock, and the wrong call there is a suite that passes without asserting anything. T-009 reviews it with opus for the same reason, and its acceptance criteria are mutation checks on a scratch copy of the tree rather than a reading of the diff. Everything else is sonnet: ordinary implementation and review against a frozen design.

DOCS THE ORCHESTRATOR OWNS, NOT A SUB-AGENT — CLAUDE.md:104 ("There is no test framework and the project does not want one") and .claude/ENVIRONMENT.md §"Verification without a test framework" both become false the moment this run lands, and every future agent reads them. They are workflow configuration, so no task below has them in allowed_paths. Update them yourself after T-011 approves, as a tier-1 doc change. README.md does not mention the policy today and is in T-010's paths.

ESCAPE HATCH FIRST — T-001 installs and proves the runner before any test is written, so a broken toolchain surfaces as one failed devops task rather than as four dispatchers reporting tests they could not run. And T-001's own install criterion is that better-sqlite3 still loads afterwards: the realistic way this run damages the user's setup is an npm install under the wrong Node rebuilding the native addon, breaking their server on its next restart.

tasks.title: The flight manager suite: state transitions, pause detection, track-derived duration
tasks.goal: The centrepiece of the run. Test src/flightManager.ts's FlightManager class end to end at its own boundary: feed it SimFrames through onFrame/setPaused/onCrash/onSimDisconnect under a fake clock (design §5) with './db' and './airports' mocked (design §6), and assert on the recorded calls to insertFlight/insertPoint/closeFlight/linkFlightToPlannedLeg/recordPlannedLegArrival and on the public appState and getPlannedLegStatus(). Do NOT modify src/flightManager.ts — design §7 forbids source changes outside src/airports.ts, and the class is already testable through mocks and fake timers. Every assertion about a duration must come from advancing the fake clock, never from a real wait. The named behaviours below are the user's stated reason for this run; treat the acceptance list as the specification.
acceptance_criteria: STATE — IDLE to FLYING requires exactly AIRBORNE_DEBOUNCE_FRAMES (3) consecutive qualifying frames: two qualifying frames produce no insertFlight call; the third does. A non-qualifying frame between them resets the streak and a following two qualifying frames still produce no flight.

STATE — a frame with simRunning === 3 (slew) never starts a flight, however many are fed; a frame with onGround true never starts one; a frame with airspeedKnots === 30 never starts one (the guard is strictly greater than 30) while 31 does.

STATE — FLYING to IDLE requires exactly LANDED_DEBOUNCE_FRAMES (10) consecutive frames with onGround && groundSpeedKnots < 5: nine produce no closeFlight, the tenth does; one frame with groundSpeedKnots === 5 resets the streak.
STATE — simRunning === 0 ends a FLYING flight immediately with one closeFlight call, and is a silent no-op when IDLE (no closeFlight, no throw).

STATE — onCrash() and onSimDisconnect() each end a FLYING flight using the last frame's coordinates (asserted on closeFlight's lat/lon arguments), and are no-ops when IDLE or when no frame has ever arrived.
STATE — after endFlight, appState.flightState is 'IDLE' and appState.currentFlightId is null; after startFlight they are 'FLYING' and the id insertFlight returned.
PAUSE — setPaused(true, flags) sets appState.paused true and appState.pauseFlags to flags; setPaused(false) sets paused false and pauseFlags to 0 regardless of the flags argument.
PAUSE — frames delivered while paused record no points: after a pause spanning several RECORD_INTERVAL_MS windows, insertPoint's call count is unchanged.

PAUSE — the gap that SPANS a pause is excluded from duration even when it is shorter than MAX_COUNTED_GAP_MS. Concretely: a pause of 10 s (well under 60 s) must not appear in the duration_sec passed to closeFlight — this is the `interrupted` flag path at src/flightManager.ts:493, and it is the assertion that distinguishes pause handling from plain gap handling.
PAUSE — slew (simRunning === 3) while FLYING records no point and marks the following gap interrupted, exactly as a pause does; asserted the same way.
DURATION — insertPoint is called at most once per RECORD_INTERVAL_MS (5000): advancing 4999 ms after a point records nothing, advancing 5000 ms records one.

DURATION — duration_sec passed to closeFlight equals the sum of the counted inter-point gaps plus the tail interval, computed by hand in the test from the clock advances, not read back from the implementation. Give at least one multi-point flight where the expected number is written as a literal.
DURATION — the MAX_COUNTED_GAP_MS boundary is pinned exactly: a gap of exactly 60000 ms IS counted, a gap of 60001 ms is NOT.

DURATION — the tail interval between the last recorded point and endFlight is counted when the flight was not interrupted and the tail is <= MAX_COUNTED_GAP_MS, and excluded when either condition fails; both branches asserted.

DURATION — a flight whose wall-clock span exceeds its counted time still reports a duration_sec equal only to the counted time (the excluded-seconds path), asserted on a flight containing one over-long gap.

ACCUMULATORS — closeFlight receives distance rounded to Math.round(d*10)/10, max altitude and max airspeed as the running maxima across recorded points only (a higher value seen in a frame that was NOT recorded must not raise them), and point_count equal to the number of insertPoint calls.

PLANNED LEG — getPlannedLegStatus() returns null while unlinked. After an auto-link, it returns the next waypoint chosen by cross-track distance (a position beside the first segment of a 4-waypoint route names waypoint[1], a position beside the last segment names the destination) and remainingDistanceNm equal to the direct distance to that waypoint plus the chain to the destination, rounded to one decimal.

PLANNED LEG — getPlannedLegStatus() picks the correct segment for a route crossing the antimeridian (waypoints at 179.5°E and 179.5°W), i.e. lonDeltaDeg is exercised and the answer is not the ~360°-wide one.

PLANNED LEG — auto-link: a MATCHED result calls linkFlightToPlannedLeg(flightId, legId, 'auto') exactly once and populates the status cache; a refusal calls it zero times and leaves getPlannedLegStatus() null; and a THROW from getActiveTripId, getPlannedLegCandidatesForActiveTrip, getPlannedLegById or linkFlightToPlannedLeg leaves the flight recorded (insertFlight already called, no rethrow out of onFrame) and unlinked. Assert all four throw sites.

PLANNED LEG — arrival: landing within ARRIVAL_RADIUS_NM records 'flown', landing beyond it records 'diverted', both with deviation rounded to Math.round(d*10)/10, and neither unlinks the flight; a throw from recordPlannedLegArrival does not propagate out of endFlight.
PLANNED LEG — refreshPlannedLegForFlight(id) is a no-op for an id that is not the current flight, clears the cache when getFlightPlannedLegId returns null, and rebuilds it when it returns a leg.

HERMETIC — the test file mocks './db' and './airports'; `grep -n "better-sqlite3\|flights.db" <test files>` finds nothing, and no real timer wait is used (`grep -n "await new Promise\|setTimeout(" <test files>` finds nothing outside fake-timer helpers).

`npx vitest run` over these files exits 0 with 0 failed and 0 skipped, and finishes in under 10 seconds despite simulating flights of tens of minutes — report the measured time as the evidence that the clock is faked.
`npx tsc` exits 0, `npm run build` exits 0, `npm test` exits 0, and `git diff --stat src/flightManager.ts` is empty.

tasks.title: Review phase 3 — the flight manager suite, by mutation
tasks.goal: This is the review that decides whether the run delivered what the user asked for. A flight-manager suite that passes because it asserts nothing meaningful is the expensive failure mode, and it is invisible in a green run and nearly invisible in a diff. Judge it by mutating a scratch copy of the source and confirming the suite notices. Copy the tree to the scratchpad first (cp -r); never mutate the repo in place, and never touch the live server or flights.db.
acceptance_criteria: Re-ran `npm test`, `npx tsc` and `npm run build`; all exit 0. Reported the suite's total wall-clock time and confirmed it is under the 10 s the task claimed.
MUTATION 1 — AIRBORNE_DEBOUNCE_FRAMES 3 -> 2 in the scratch copy makes at least one named test fail.
MUTATION 2 — LANDED_DEBOUNCE_FRAMES 10 -> 9 makes at least one named test fail.
MUTATION 3 — MAX_COUNTED_GAP_MS 60_000 -> 600_000 makes at least one named test fail.

MUTATION 4 — deleting the `!this.interrupted &&` guard at src/flightManager.ts:493 (writePoint's gap accumulation) makes at least one PAUSE test fail. This is the mutation that proves pause detection is genuinely covered rather than incidentally covered.
MUTATION 5 — deleting the `!this.interrupted &&` guard in endFlight's tail-interval line (src/flightManager.ts:276) makes at least one DURATION test fail.
MUTATION 6 — changing the arrival comparison `deviationNm <= ARRIVAL_RADIUS_NM` to `<` makes at least one PLANNED LEG test fail.
MUTATION 7 — changing RECORD_INTERVAL_MS 5000 -> 1000 makes at least one DURATION test fail.
MUTATION 8 — replacing crossTrackNm's lonDeltaDeg calls with raw longitude subtraction makes the antimeridian getPlannedLegStatus test fail.
For each of the eight mutations, name the specific test that failed. Any mutation that leaves the suite green is a request_changes with that mutation quoted.
Restored/discarded the scratch copy and confirmed `git status --porcelain` in the real repo shows only T-008's allowed_paths; `git diff src/flightManager.ts` is empty.
md5sum of flights.db unchanged, and the user's server on port 3000 was never stopped, restarted or rebuilt over mid-edit.

tasks.title: Ship: finalise npm scripts, decide test:watch, update README, prove build and Docker are undisturbed
tasks.goal: Wire the run into the project's surface. Confirm `npm test` runs the whole suite in one non-interactive command. Make the `test:watch` call per design §9 and this project's temperament — it resists tooling, so add it only if it is a one-line script and say plainly in the report why you did or did not; do not add coverage, reporters, CI config, or a pretest hook. Document how to run the tests in README.md in a short paragraph next to the existing build/run instructions. Then prove the two things a new devDependency can break: `npm run build`, and the Docker server stage, which copies only package*.json, tsconfig.json and src/.
acceptance_criteria: `timeout 180 npm test` exits 0, runs every test file added in this run, and reports the total test count. Quote the summary line.
package.json's scripts block contains `test`, and contains `test:watch` if and only if the report justifies it in one sentence. No coverage script, no pretest/posttest hook, no CI config file added.
`npm run build` exits 0. `npx tsc` exits 0. `ls dist | grep -i test` finds nothing.

Docker server stage simulation: copy package.json, package-lock.json, tsconfig.json and src/ into a scratch dir, `npm ci`, `npm run build:server` — exit 0. If it fails, that is the Dockerfile-compatibility bug this criterion exists to catch; report it rather than editing the Dockerfile (it is outside allowed_paths).

`npm ci --omit=dev` in a scratch dir does NOT install vitest (it is a devDependency) — confirm with `npm ls vitest` there, which must report it as missing/empty. This is what keeps the runtime image unchanged.
`node -e "require('better-sqlite3')"` exits 0 and `npm ls better-sqlite3` reports the same version as at the start of the run.
README.md gains a short, accurate description of how to run the tests, consistent with the actual script names; no claim in it is untrue (CLAUDE.md requires README stay accurate).
`git status --porcelain` shows only files inside this run's allowed_paths across all tasks; no coverage/, .vitest/ or scratch artefact is untracked.
md5sum of flights.db unchanged; the live server was not stopped or restarted.

tasks.title: Review phase 4 — ship readiness
tasks.goal: Re-run T-010's evidence and read the whole run's diff once, end to end, as the last chance to catch something that slipped between phases: a stray file, an untrue README sentence, a script that hangs in watch mode, or a source change outside src/airports.ts.
acceptance_criteria: Re-ran `timeout 180 npm test`, `npm run build`, `npx tsc`, the Docker server-stage simulation and the `npm ci --omit=dev` check; all pass as reported.
`git diff --stat` for the whole run shows exactly one changed file under src/ that is not a test file — src/airports.ts — and its diff matches design §7.
Read README.md's new paragraph and confirmed every command in it actually works when run.
Confirmed `npm test` is non-interactive (exits on its own, not 124 under timeout) and that watch mode, if added, is a separate script.
Confirmed nothing in the run reads or writes flights.db, makes a network request, or writes outside tmp; md5sum of flights.db unchanged.
Flagged to the Orchestrator that CLAUDE.md:104 and .claude/ENVIRONMENT.md's "Verification without a test framework" section are now false and are outside every task's allowed_paths by design.
